design.quote: We used a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, crossover design in 22 healthy participants (11 women, 11 men) who received placebo and DMT (0.6, 1.2, 1.8, and 2.4 mg/min) over an infusion duration of 120 min.
design.text: A double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, crossover study of continuous DMT infusions in 22 healthy participants.

findings.quote: The present study documented the presence of acute pharmacological tolerance to the continuous administration of DMT.
findings.text: The study documented that people develop acute pharmacological tolerance to DMT when it is administered continuously.

findings.quote: We observed moderate acute tolerance to subjective effects of DMT, indicated by clockwise hysteresis (Fig.). Specifically, subjective effects showed no increase from 30 to 120 min, despite increasing plasma concentrations.
findings.text: Moderate acute tolerance to the subjective effects of DMT was observed, as these effects did not increase between 30 and 120 minutes even though plasma concentrations continued to rise.

findings.quote: Our findings and others do not support the view that DMT exerts no tolerance, in contrast to other psychedelics. In fact, little to no acute pharmacological tolerance is observed with LSD, psilocybin, or mescaline.
findings.text: The findings do not support the view that DMT does not cause tolerance, unlike LSD, psilocybin, or mescaline, where little to no acute pharmacological tolerance is observed.

limits.quote: The study used a highly controlled setting and included only healthy participants. Thus, subjects in different environments and patients with psychiatric disorders may respond differently to DMT.
limits.text: The study only included healthy participants in a highly controlled setting, so patients with psychiatric disorders or people in different environments might have different responses.
